<div class="clt-lesson batch-lesson" data-lesson="regression"><h2 id="learning-goals">What are we trying to understand?</h2><p><strong>How can a line summarize a relationship, and how much should we trust its predictions?</strong></p><p>Use the same study-hours and attention-score examples from correlation. Fit the least-squares line, inspect individual residuals, and move the prediction point within and beyond the observed range.</p><div class="clt-overview"><strong>Learning goals</strong><ol><li>Interpret the fitted slope and intercept in context.</li><li>Calculate and interpret residuals.</li><li>Explain least squares and R².</li><li>Distinguish interpolation, extrapolation and causal interpretation.</li></ol></div><h2 id="explore">Make a prediction and explore</h2><section class="clt-simulator"><p>Predict how a low-scoring observation at high study hours might change the fitted line.</p><div class="controls"><div><label for="slope">Underlying linear pattern: <output id="slope-v">3</output></label><input id="slope" type="range" min="-4" max="4" step="1" value="3"></div><div><label for="noise">Scatter multiplier: <output id="noise-v">2</output></label><input id="noise" type="range" min="1" max="4" step="1" value="2"></div><div><label for="outlier">Additional observation</label><select id="outlier"><option value="none">None</option><option value="high">High score at 11 hours</option><option value="low">Low score at 11 hours</option></select></div><div><label for="prediction">Predict at study hours: <output id="prediction-v">6</output></label><input id="prediction" type="range" min="0" max="14" step="1" value="6"></div></div><div class="metrics"><div class="metric"><span>Slope</span><strong id="b">—</strong></div><div class="metric"><span>Intercept</span><strong id="a">—</strong></div><div class="metric"><span>R²</span><strong id="r2">—</strong></div><div class="metric"><span>Predicted score</span><strong id="pred">—</strong></div><div class="metric"><span>Residual sum of squares</span><strong id="sse">—</strong></div><div class="metric"><span>Residual standard error</span><strong id="rmse">—</strong></div></div><div id="chart" class="plot"></div><p class="note">Dark line: least-squares fit. Open circle: selected prediction (if within plot limits).</p><p id="equation"></p><p id="warning" class="formula" role="status"></p><details><summary>View fitted values and residuals</summary><table class="data-table"><caption>Residual = actual − fitted</caption><thead><tr><th scope="col">Hours</th><th scope="col">Actual</th><th scope="col">Fitted</th><th scope="col">Residual</th></tr></thead><tbody id="residual-table"></tbody></table></details></section><h2 id="interpret">Interpret what you find</h2><ol><li>Use the starting data. Interpret the slope in attention-score points per study hour.</li><li>Increase noise. Compare residual lengths, residual standard error and R².</li><li>Add the low outlier and compare the slope with the original fit.</li><li>Predict at 6 and 14 hours. Explain why the second prediction needs additional caution.</li></ol><h2 id="explanation">What is the method telling us?</h2><div class="formula">ŷ = b₀ + b₁x<br>Residual = y − ŷ<br>Least squares minimizes Σ residual²<br>R² = 1 − SSE / total SS</div><p>The slope is the predicted change in score per additional hour, not necessarily a causal effect. The intercept is the predicted score at zero hours; it may not be substantively meaningful if zero is outside the data. R² describes the proportion of observed outcome variation accounted for by this fitted linear model. Residual standard error is √[SSE/(n−2)]. For inference, assess linearity, independent errors, constant variance and normality of errors as appropriate. A prediction is not a guarantee and extrapolation beyond the observed x range can be misleading.</p><h2 id="knowledge-check">Check your understanding</h2><p>Choose an answer, then check your reasoning.
